core: Artificial intelligence, intelligent agents and computational models
Programming, algorithms, software and computer systems
Mathematics, logic, probability, statistics and data modelling
Machine learning, neural networks, deep learning and reinforcement learning
Cognition, psychology, neuroscience, perception and learning
Robotics, autonomous systems, computer vision and human-centred design
Ethics, philosophy and societal impact of artificial intelligence
Experimental design, research methods, academic communication and independent research
adjacent: Computational AI and autonomous intelligent systems
Applications of AI in science and society
questions: How can intelligent systems learn, reason, plan and act?
What can computational models reveal about human thought, perception, language and the brain?
How should AI systems be designed and evaluated for people and society?

alternatives.label: Artificial Intelligence, Cognition & Intelligent Systems
alternatives.concept: Study how intelligent systems learn, reason and act, alongside how people perceive, think and use language. Combine machine learning and robotics with experiments and research on human cognition.
alternatives.labelReason: The curriculum integrates computational AI with substantial cognitive-science and intelligent-systems study, so the label names all three organising elements.
progression: Programming, brain and behaviour, data and calculus come first. Linear algebra and statistical learning precede neural networks, and decision models precede reinforcement learning.

alternatives.label: Computational AI & autonomous systems
alternatives.concept: Build computational systems that learn and act. Combine software development, algorithms and computer infrastructure with optimisation, computer vision and reinforcement learning.
alternatives.labelReason: The curriculum's dense programming, algorithms, mathematics, learning, optimisation and robotics sequence supports a computational and autonomous-systems label.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the broad closest match and the cognitive route, this curriculum replaces much of the psychology, neuroscience and philosophy content with databases, networks, software development, advanced algorithms, reinforcement learning and numerical methods.
progression: Programming, data and mathematics support software, algorithms and robotics. Data structures precede advanced algorithms. Statistical learning and linear algebra precede neural networks.

alternatives.label: Cognitive AI, language & neuroscience
alternatives.concept: Study language, perception and cognition through neuroscience, psychology and philosophy. Use statistics, machine learning and experiments to investigate behaviour and compare it with computational approaches.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed programme combines AI methods with a sustained sequence in cognitive science, neuroscience, psychology, language and philosophy.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the broad and computational alternatives, this route gives substantially greater weight to neurobiology, lifespan and social psychology, perception, higher cognition, psycholinguistics, philosophy of mind, agency and advanced behavioural research.
progression: Brain and behaviour precedes psycholinguistics, perception and advanced cognition. Data handling, statistics and linear algebra support neural networks and evidence synthesis.

candidates.label: Computational AI and autonomous intelligent systems

selection.assessment: The broad option integrates the technical and cognitive foundations. The computational option adds software infrastructure and advanced algorithms. The cognitive option develops a sustained sequence in perception, language, development and philosophy of mind. Each option differs by at least four courses in each direction.

blocks: Both provide a foundational introduction to programming for later computational study.
Both develop systematic software design and implementation practices.
Advanced Algorithms develops systematic computational problem solving; it is more algorithmically specialised than the UvA course.
Both use probabilistic models to reason under uncertainty. UCR covers Bayesian networks within a broader course on how agents make decisions.
Both directly cover data structures, algorithms and computational complexity.
Both use mathematical optimisation methods for computational and AI problems.
Both provide a dedicated introduction to machine-learning methods and model evaluation.
Both provide substantial neural-network theory and implementation, with UCR also extending into deep learning.
Both study robotics. UCR concentrates on kinematics, grasping and planning robot motion. The UvA overview describes a course on robots that learn.
Both directly cover image processing and computer-vision methods.
Both cover single-variable calculus, including differentiation, integration and mathematical problem solving.
Both develop linear-algebra foundations through matrices, vectors and transformations.
Both develop formal logic and discrete reasoning for computing and AI.
Both combine probability and statistical inference for data-driven modelling.
Both study aspects of language processing. UCR examines human language production, comprehension and acquisition. UvA builds computational language-processing methods.
Both ask philosophical questions about mind and intelligence. UvA also addresses ethics as part of its AI curriculum.
Both consider fairness, safety and societal impacts of AI. UCR also uses ethical theory and psychology to study human interaction with AI.
Both provide explicit first-year academic and professional formation; UCR PPD is broader than the AI-specific practicum.

notes.text: The UCR options combine computing and AI with mathematics, cognition or software systems. The UvA curriculum includes dedicated work in computational language processing, running machine-learning systems and an 18 EC graduation project.

audience.programmeDescription: Artificial Intelligence at the University of Amsterdam combines mathematics and computing with the study of cognition, language and how intelligent systems learn.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The UCR schedules explore related AI directions. The later UvA course requirements for September 2026 entrants still need confirmation.
